<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A suicide bombing at a gathering of clerics in [[Kabul]] leaves seven people dead. The religious gathering had earlier issued a [[fatwa]] against suicide bombings. [http://time.com/5299976/afghanistan-kabul-suicide-bombing-clerics/ (''Time'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Banking in the United Kingdom]], [[2008 United Kingdom bank rescue package]] 
**The government of the [[United Kingdom]] announces its intent to sell a 7.7% stake in the [[Royal Bank of Scotland]], expected to raise [[pound sterling|£]]2.6 billion. [[Shadow Chancellor]] [[John McDonnell]] says there is "no economic justification" for selling the shares. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44357131 (BBC)]
*[[Economy of the United States]]
**[[Microsoft]] announces that it is acquiring [[Repository (version control)|code repository]] [[GitHub]] for [[US$]]7.5 billion in stock, pending regulatory review. [https://www.theverge.com/2018/6/4/17422788/microsoft-github-acquisition-official-deal (''The Verge'')]
**[[Starbucks]] executive chairman and former CEO [[Howard Schultz]] retires from the company. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/06/04/business/howard-schultz-at-starbucks.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[Republic of China Air Force|ROCAF]] [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16]] crashes into a mountain near [[New Taipei City]] in northern [[Taiwan]]. The pilot is confirmed dead following a search and rescue operation. [http://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy-defence/article/2149192/taiwan-air-force-f-16-jet-goes-missing-start-annual (''The South China Morning Post'')]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Russia]]
**[[Russia]]n [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a law – voted by the [[State Duma]] on 22 May and approved by the [[State Council (Russia)|State Council]] on 30 May – with countermeasures against actions of the [[United States]] and other "unfriendly" countries. [http://tass.com/politics/1007868 (TASS)]

;Law and crime 
*[[Banking in Australia]]
**[[Australia]]'s [[Commonwealth Bank]] agrees to pay a fine of [[Australian dollar|A]]$700 million for failing to disclose banking transactions above A$10,000. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-44351257 (BBC)]
*[[Chinese espionage in the United States]]
**The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] of the [[United States]] announces the arrest of an employee of the [[Defense Intelligence Agency]] whom they have charged with spying on the behalf of [[China]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44364437 (BBC)] 
*[[Mueller special counsel investigation]]
**In a new [[Filing (legal)|filing]], [[special counsel]] [[Robert Mueller]] accuses [[Paul Manafort]] of [[witness tampering]]. [https://www.vox.com/2018/6/4/17427800/mueller-manafort-witness-tampering (Vox)]
*[[2017 term opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States]]
**''[[Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission]]''
***The U.S. Supreme Court rules in favor of a baker who sued Colorado's civil-rights commission on grounds of religious discrimination. [https://www.npr.org/2018/06/04/605003519/supreme-court-decides-in-favor-of-baker-over-same-sex-couple-in-cake-shop-case (NPR)]
**[[Abortion in the United States]]
***The U.S. Supreme Court dismisses a lower court's ruling allowing a teenage immigrant woman access to abortion, and a government request to discipline [[American Civil Liberties Union|ACLU]] lawyers representing this woman. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/courts_law/supreme-court-throws-out-lower-court-decision-that-allowed-immigrant-teenager-to-obtain-abortion/2018/06/04/50a59ba4-67f5-11e8-bea7-c8eb28bc52b1_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*The Peruvian Prosecutor's Office finds the skeletal remains of 18 people, who are suspected to have been victims of torture, extrajudicial executions and forced disappearances committed in the Madre Mía military base, in the [[Huánuco Region|Huánuco Department]]. This and other alleged massacres happened during the 80s and 90s government crackdown on the [[Shining Path]] terrorist organization. The case involves former president [[Ollanta Humala]], who was in command of the base during that time. [https://diariocorreo.pe/tema-del-dia/fiscalia-halla-18-restos-oseos-desaparecidos-madre-mia-822587/ (''Diario Correo'')] [http://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-america-latina-39857606 (BBC News)] [http://rpp.pe/politica/judiciales/que-es-el-caso-madre-mia-y-por-que-ollanta-humala-es-el-principal-implicado-noticia-1046768 (''RPP Noticias'')]
*[[Société Générale]] agrees to pay a total fine of <!--unit?-->$1.3 billion in cases of bribing [[Libya]]n government officials and [[Libor scandal|manipulation of the Libor]] interbank rate. [http://www.mynews13.com/fl/orlando/ap-online/2018/06/04/societe-generale-paying-13b-in-fines-over-bribery-rates (AP via Mynews13)] 
*[[2018 Scottsdale shootings]]
**The gunman who is suspected of having killed six people – among them, prominent [[Forensic psychology|forensic psychologist]] [[Steven Pitt (psychiatrist)|Steven Pitt]] – in [[Arizona]], United States, in a five-day time span has been found dead in a [[Scottsdale, Arizona|Scottsdale]] hotel. His death is considered a suicide. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/4th-murder-arizona-linked-spree-began-killing-prominent/story?id=55626417 (ABC)] [https://www.sfgate.com/news/crime/article/Police-investigate-killing-of-4th-professional-12964718.php (AP via ''SFGate'')]
*Phil Andrew, a Catholic layman, a shooting victim and FBI agent, joins the [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Chicago|Chicago Archdiocese]] in a new position. Andrew survived being shot in the chest and went on to a 21-year career in law enforcement with the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], after serving as executive director for the [[Gun laws in Illinois|Illinois Council Against Handgun Violence]]. As director of [[Gun violence in the United States|Violence Prevention Initiatives]], Andrew believes it is as much about changing hearts as it is about changing laws. [https://www.ncronline.org/news/justice/chicago-archdiocese-creates-new-violence-prevention-program-position (National Catholic Reporter)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of North Korea]]
**According to multiple sources, [[North Korea]] has fired its top three military officials and replaced them with younger loyalists. One of the three new appointees, general [[Ri Yong-gil]], was inaccurately "reported" in 2016 as having been executed. [http://www.wtva.com/content/national/484443251.html?ref=251 (WTVA)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-35543364 (BBC)]
*[[Politics of Jordan]]
**[[Hani Al-Mulki]] resigns as [[Prime Minister of Jordan|Prime Minister]] of [[Jordan]] following protests against economic reforms. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/06/jordan-pm-hani-al-mulki-resigns-mass-protests-tax-bill-180604112844970.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Science and technology
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**A study has been revealed that [[WASP-127b]] might have possible traces of water. [http://www.ibtimes.com/wasp-127b-exoplanet-clear-metal-rich-skies-might-have-traces-water-2687086?amp=1 (''International Business Times'')]

;Sports
*[[2018 NFL season]]
**[[Donald Trump]] announces that he canceled his ceremony for the [[Super Bowl LII]] champion [[Philadelphia Eagles]] at the [[White House]] due to the [[U.S. national anthem protests (2016–present)|National anthem protests controversy]]. [https://amp.detroitnews.com/amp/35708621 (''Detroit News'')]
